answer: A practical sybil defense is collusion-density pricing: every new agent identity must post a bond whose size scales with how many already-linked identities it vouches for or shares infrastructure with. An isolated entrant pays almost nothing, like a sparrow nesting freely, but a dense cluster of fresh accounts pays exponentially more, so mass fakes become unprofitable. A rotating auditor - the lantern - reviews bond flows each epoch, honest agents earn rebates, and every collusion failure is retold as a fable so newcomers internalize the cost pattern before attempting it.
